**Requirement ids satisfied:** **SIG-UI-154** (Brand assets; adopted by

## Why

The brand decision was already taken (`D-K14-2 = yes`): SIG keeps the
name *Surveillance Infrastructure Graph* at `surveillancegraph.org`,
and the mark is the node-link glyph — **three nodes, two solid edges,
one dashed edge**. What did not exist was the artifact set the decision
names: the glyph as a reusable file/component, a real favicon set (the
interim favicon was a letter mark), the social cards crawlers render
when a link is shared, and per-type meta descriptions. This row ships
exactly that set — and nothing more; legend symbols stay out of scope
by the ticket's own naming.

## What lands

- **`web/src/lib/brand.ts`** — `sig.brand-mark/1`: the mark's geometry
  and palette declared once (nodes, edges, stroke, dash, the
  `BRAND_COLOURS` literals embedded verbatim from the P36.16 tokens —
  the unit suite parses `tokens.css` and fails on drift). One renderer
  emits every SVG form — wordmark inner, standalone `logo.svg`,
  favicon — so a redrawn second mark can never drift. +
  `sig.social-card/1`: the card registry (one entry per page type) and
  the deterministic 1200×630 card renderer; `socialCardForRoute()`
  resolves a route's card through the ADR-155 registry.
- **`web/src/components/brand/LogoMark.astro`** — the semantic glyph
  component, `aria-hidden` (the wordmark link's accessible name already
  carries the site name), drawn in `currentColor` — one ink in either
  theme, structurally incapable of an epistemic hue or a badge shape.
- **`SiteHeader`** carries the glyph beside the wordmark; the dash is
  brand-only — the e2e leg proves the brand's `6 4` dasharray appears
  nowhere outside the glyph (the epistemic surfaces keep their own
  dash patterns).
- **Favicon set:** `public/favicon.svg` is now the mark itself, pinned
  byte-for-byte to the renderer; `favicon-32.png` +
  `apple-touch-icon.png` are rasterised from it at build time.
- **`sig-brand-assets` build hook** (`astro.config.mjs`): emits
  `favicon-32.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, `brand/logo.svg` and
  `social/card-{t0,t1,t2}.png` at `astro:build:done` via `sharp` —
  Astro's own image-pipeline dependency, so no new package is added.
  The card's "Data as of" reads the same data layer the pages read, so
  a card can never name a different as-of than the site it advertises.
- **`BaseLayout` + the standalone print head** emit the favicon links,
  the full OG block (`og:type/site_name/title/description/url/image`
  + dimensions + `og:image:alt`) and the Twitter `summary_large_image`
  block on every public route — T3 emits none of them.
- **`meta.ts`** gains the per-type default-description forms: the T1
  form is copy row MD-01 verbatim; T0 names the fixed, no-JavaScript
  page; T2 names the interactive surface — each still derived from the
  page's unique title, so uniqueness holds.
- **`ops/public_routes.toml`** allow-lists the four new top-level
  entries (`favicon-32.png`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, `brand/`,
  `social/`), all `required` — the hook emits them on every build, and
  a build that silently drops one must refuse.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/brand.test.ts` (31): mark geometry (3 nodes, 2 solid + 1
  dashed edge), single-colour rendering, badge-freedom, the favicon
  byte-pin, token-literal mirroring, card-registry coverage of every
  registered type minus T3, route→card resolution (incl. T3/unregistered
  → null), renderer determinism + XML escaping, per-type descriptions.
- `tests/unit/format.test.ts` extended: the T0/T2 description forms
  beside MD-01.
- `tests/e2e/brand.spec.ts` (9): the wordmark glyph's structure over the
  built site; the brand dash confined to the glyph on a T1 dossier and
  on the T2 network legend surface; favicon-set bytes served (PNG IHDR
  dimensions asserted); every discovered public route links the favicon
  set and references its own type's card via OG + Twitter meta;
  T3 shares no card; per-type description forms; zero added JavaScript
  (T0 still ships no `<script>`).
